clue.text: Economist goes by jet - he needs to strike while the iron is hot

definitions.text: he needs to strike while the iron is hot

indicators.note: to go by something is to sit beside it, so the economist's name is placed next to the colour word

blocks.note: jet is a deep glossy black
Adam Smith, author of The Wealth of Nations

explanation.surface: An economist flying by jet, with a proverb about seizing the moment tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb about striking while the iron is hot is meant literally here: it describes the man at the forge.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith hammers metal at the forge, and must strike while the heated metal is still workable.

clue.text: Sign worker installed inside shed

indicators.note: something installed inside is fitted within, so one word sits in the other

blocks.note: a sign of the zodiac
a worker ant

explanation.surface: A signwriter's employee fitted into a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed built against a wall, its roof resting on it.

clue.text: Comprehensive head initially overwhelmed by abuse

indicators.note: initially keeps just the opening letter of the word before it
being overwhelmed means being engulfed, so the letter is swallowed by the word

blocks.note: a jeering whistle or shout
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A headteacher overwhelmed by a torrent of abuse, in a sweeping account.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch-all covers every case, so it is all-embracing or comprehensive.

clue.text: Sort of house, not flat

blocks.note: first meaning: a building type
second meaning: on more than one plane

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not flat' looks like 'not an apartment', fitting the house theme, but means uneven.
explanation.definitionFit: A split-level home has floors at staggered heights, and anything so arranged is uneven rather than level.

clue.text: Establish how visiting President, for one, should be received

definitions.text: how visiting President, for one, should be received

blocks.note: first meaning: install in office

blocks.clueFragment: how visiting President, for one, should be received
blocks.note: second meaning, as two words: with full ceremony

explanation.surface: Protocol for a foreign head of state's official visit.
explanation.definitionFit: To instate is to install someone in a post, and a head of state is received with pomp, in state.

clue.text: Hurt right inside thigh

indicators.note: inside places the letter within the word for the meat

blocks.note: the ham is the back of the thigh
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An injury on the inner right thigh, like a pulled muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurt someone is to harm them; the two verbs are close synonyms.

clue.text: Brave and strong, like Van Gogh, partly

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud or strong
the painter cut off part of one ear, so was partly without one

explanation.surface: Praise for the painter as bold and powerful, at least in part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partly' seems to qualify the praise; it refers to the part of the ear he lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearless and brave both describe a person who shows no fright in danger.

clue.text: Establishes legal digest

blocks.note: first meaning: sets up, a verb
second meaning: a summary of law, as in Justinian's

explanation.surface: Setting up a summary of the law.
explanation.definitionFit: To institute is to set up, and the Institutes are classic textbooks of Roman law.

clue.text: A rigid back

blocks.note: taken as written
stern means strict or unbending

explanation.surface: A stiff back, the kind a doctor might note.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical adverb for towards the rear of a ship, so going back.

clue.text: Flog anklebone of Greek undergoing torture

blocks.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
the talus is the bone of the ankle joint

explanation.surface: A grim scene of beating and bone-breaking inflicted on some tortured Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth he stood in water under fruit he could never reach, the source of the word tantalise.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical king was punished in Hades with endless thirst and hunger, a classic eternal torment.

clue.text: Languish in jail, perhaps, on private bunk

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece written on another follows it, so the soldier comes first

blocks.note: Tommy Atkins, slang for a British private soldier
to rot in jail is to languish there; perhaps marks it as one example

explanation.surface: A soldier left to waste away in the cells on his prison bunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' seems to be a prison bed but means nonsense, short for bunkum.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommyrot and bunk are both informal words for foolish talk or nonsense.

clue.text: Artistic conclusion a medic backs

indicators.note: going backwards, the short phrase is read from its last letter to its first

blocks.note: taken as written
doc is short for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor supporting the finale of some artistic work.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the closing passage of a musical piece, or a concluding section of any work.

clue.text: The prospect of the rack?

blocks.note: surface reading: the dread of being stretched on a torture device
setter's reading: rack is drifting cloud, and a prospect is a view of a scene

explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospect' looks like anticipation and 'rack' like torture; both have scenic senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Rack is an old word for wind-driven cloud, so a view of it is a picture of the sky.

clue.text: We should look forward to something, and be realistic

definitions.text: We should look forward to something

blocks.clueFragment: We should look forward to something
blocks.note: first meaning: literally, let us turn our faces towards a thing
second meaning: the idiom for admitting an unwelcome truth

explanation.surface: A pep talk urging hope for the future but also some realism.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces a blunt admission, while its literal sense is turning to meet something head on.

clue.text: I bet, to make unknown amount with cash

blocks.note: to form is to make
y is an algebraic unknown quantity
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: A gambler placing a stake in cash, hoping to win an unknown sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce a personal opinion: in my view, I reckon.

clue.text: Survive being dismissed, as it happens

blocks.note: a batsman who is dismissed is out
a live broadcast is shown as it happens

explanation.surface: Getting through the sack, as it turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As it happens' looks like a filler phrase meaning 'by chance'; it is the broadcasting sense, in real time.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlive something is to last beyond it, which is to survive it.

clue.text: With discretion, brought up name that's on tip of tongue

indicators.note: in a down answer, brought up means written from bottom to top

blocks.note: discernment in choosing what is fitting
to dub is to name

explanation.surface: Discreetly mentioning a name you can almost but not quite recall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the tip of the tongue' is the idiom for a word you nearly remember; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensory receptors for flavour sit on the tongue, many of them at its front end.

clue.text: Jerky start in crossing

indicators.note: jerky movement is jolting and irregular, so these letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: the two words taken as letters

explanation.surface: A jolting departure as one begins to cross over.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of passing across or through from one side to another.

clue.text: Peerless item unchosen, remarkably

indicators.note: remarkably implies something surprising has happened to the letters, here a rearrangement

blocks.note: taken as letters

explanation.surface: An outstanding piece left oddly unpicked.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonesuch is a person or thing without equal, an archaic word for a paragon.

clue.text: Elects to play by ear at first on this?

definitions.text: Elects to play by ear at first on this?

indicators.note: at first keeps only the opening letter of the word before it
letters set to play are let loose to move about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as letters
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A musician choosing to play an instrument by ear.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: an instrument one might choose to play by ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A celeste, or celesta, is a keyboard instrument whose hammers strike metal plates.

clue.text: This I'll site foolishly in non alcoholic surroundings?

definitions.text: This I'll site foolishly in non alcoholic surroundings?

indicators.note: doing something foolishly means doing it wrongly, so the letters end up jumbled
placing one thing in another puts the jumbled letters inside the outer word

blocks.note: the letters of these words, rearranged
a dry area or event has no alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone planning to build a whisky works in a teetotal district, and admitting it is daft.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: building a plant for spirits in a dry area would be foolish. DRY is split around the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A distillery makes spirits, so putting one in a teetotal place would be a foolish choice of location.

clue.text: Anti-American slogan showing sense

blocks.note: a protest chant rejecting the United States

explanation.surface: A protest banner that might or might not show good judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is informal British English for practical intelligence or common sense.

clue.text: Political grouping has succeeded in producing harmony

indicators.note: a word that has something holds it within, so the letter sits inside

blocks.note: a union of states or parties
s is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A party alliance that has won by achieving consensus.
explanation.walkthrough: UNISON is also the name of a large British trade union, which adds to the political surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means in perfect agreement, as voices singing the same note.

clue.text: Division revealed when outfit takes the plunge?

definitions.text: revealed when outfit takes the plunge?

blocks.note: first meaning: a split or separation

blocks.clueFragment: revealed when outfit takes the plunge?
blocks.note: second meaning: what a plunging neckline shows

explanation.surface: Someone diving into water while their swimsuit gives way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes the plunge' sounds like a dive or a bold decision, but a plunging dress has a deep low neckline.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a split or rift, and also the hollow between breasts exposed by a low-cut top.

clue.text: Continuous bad feeling in teachers' centre

indicators.note: the centre is the middle portion, so only the inner letters are kept

blocks.note: the central four of the eight letters

explanation.surface: Lingering resentment in the staff room.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull, persistent pain, a steady unpleasant sensation.

clue.text: Sum at first remaining inflated for piece of jewelry

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the preceding word only

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a balloon still inflated has not burst

explanation.surface: An accountant's sum somehow puffed up into the price of a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunburst is a brooch whose gems radiate outward like rays of the sun.

clue.text: Toby's master works in a corporation

indicators.note: to work something in is to insert it, so the small word goes inside the name

blocks.note: Toby is the dog in the Punch and Judy puppet show
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog's owner employed in some big company.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch and Judy is a traditional British seaside puppet show; 'corporation' is an old jokey word for a big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is dated humorous slang for a large stomach, the same as a pot belly.

clue.text: The sum - subtract half of this, initially, from perfect answer

indicators.note: subtracting takes letters away from the phrase that follows

blocks.note: the first two of the four letters of this
the very thing is exactly what is wanted

explanation.surface: A maths instruction for taking part of a quantity from a total.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' says which half: the front two letters of 'this' come off the front of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The sum of things is the whole lot, every part of it taken together.
